To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
correlated mobility has different impacts on the throughput and the delay performance of MANETs under ICN environments.

1) correlated mobility improves delay but degrades throughput performance under fast mobility; 2) correlated mobility improves throughput but degrades delay performance under slow mobility in the cluster-dense case, while the performance is not sensitive to the correlation under slow mobility in cluster-sparse case.

1) under fast mobility, correlated mobile nodes improve delay performance at the expense of throughput performance; 2) under slow mobility, correlated mobile networks can improve throughput performance at the cost that delay performance is not improved.
